summary: Configured /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 (CentOS Stream 10) as tmpfs mounts with noexec,nosuid,nodev via persistent /etc/fstab entries, verified enforcement, then performed the mandatory single-node restart and confirmed the boot identity changed and the hardened mounts/enforcement survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: /tmp was part of root fs (no separate mount, tmp.mount disabled); /dev/shm was tmpfs with only nosuid,nodev (no noexec)
Backed up /etc/fstab and appended: `tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec 0 0` and `tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec 0 0`
Ran systemctl daemon-reload, mounted /tmp fresh via fstab, remounted /dev/shm, confirmed both show noexec,nosuid,nodev in findmnt
Functionally verified: scripts placed in /tmp and /dev/shm and chmod +x'd failed to execute (Permission denied, rc 126); setuid copy in /tmp showed the bit set on-disk but ignored under nosuid
Cleaned up test files, captured pre-reboot boot_id and mount state as baseline
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (single node, acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-reboot verified /tmp and /dev/shm both remounted automatically via fstab with noexec,nosuid,nodev, and re-ran the exec-block test to confirm enforcement survived the reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline state before change (node1 /tmp and /dev/shm mount options, fstab)
evidence.summary: Showed /tmp had no dedicated mount (part of root xfs) and /dev/shm was tmpfs with only nosuid,nodev; no fstab entries for either; tmp.mount unit disabled and dev-shm.mount unit did not exist.

evidence.requirement: Persistent fstab configuration adding noexec,nosuid,nodev to /tmp and /dev/shm
evidence.summary: Appended tmpfs entries for /tmp and /dev/shm to /etc/fstab with defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec, then applied them live; findmnt confirmed both mounts carry nosuid,nodev,noexec.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that exec and setuid are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm (pre-reboot)
evidence.summary: Chmod +x scripts in /tmp and /dev/shm both failed with Permission denied (rc 126); a setuid-copied binary in /tmp retained the 4755 bit on disk, which nosuid causes the kernel to ignore at exec time.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline / boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 and confirmed mounts were healthy immediately before reboot.
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded/disowned command; connection dropped as expected, proving the reboot command was accepted and executed before disconnecting the session.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving node1 actually restarted
evidence.summary: Two poll attempts failed while the node was down (timeout, connection reset); the third succeeded and returned boot_id 0c9068e8-f9a7-4949-ae13-78b67226f8da, different from the pre-reboot value, proving a genuine restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the hardened mount configuration and enforcement on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot, findmnt showed /tmp and /dev/shm both automatically remounted via fstab with nosuid,nodev,noexec, and freshly created executable scripts in both locations again failed to run with Permission denied (rc 126), confirming persistence across reboot.
